expertInsight: The part that needs real practice is identity resolution. Reading about match rules teaches you the words, but you only understand reconciliation once you have watched two source records merge and seen which value won. Build one small end-to-end setup: bring data in. Map it, resolve it. Build a segment, send it somewhere. Also learn where data spaces fit, because questions about keeping brands or regions apart come up more than people expect.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Data Cloud Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: Salesforce renamed Data Cloud to Data 360, and the exam is now the Data 360 Consultant. It is a hard exam because almost nothing transfers from core Salesforce admin work. Data streams, data model objects, identity resolution and calculated insights are a new vocabulary, and the questions assume you have built with them.
bullets: 60 multiple-choice questions, plus a few unscored ones, in 105 minutes.
70% to pass, about 42 correct answers out of 60. Confirm it in the official exam guide before you book, since Salesforce updates these.
Its own vocabulary. Data streams, data lake objects, data model objects, identity resolution, calculated insights and activations.
Hands-on matters. Reading alone rarely gets people through. You need to have mapped and resolved real data.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build one complete flow in a trial org before you book: bring data in. Map it to the data model, resolve identities. Build a segment and activate it. Aim for 80% or more on practice tests, and make sure you can explain why two records merged.

examFormat.heading: Data Cloud Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: You can take the exam online with a proctor or at a test centre. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions are short scenarios. A typical one describes customer records arriving from several systems and asks how to match them, or describes an audience the marketing team wants and asks how to build and send it.
bestWayToPass: Learn identity resolution properly: Know what match rules do, what reconciliation rules do, and which value wins when two sources disagree.
Map data yourself: Bring a CSV in. Map it to data model objects, and see how keys and relationships behave.
Practise segments and activations: Build a segment, then send it to a target such as Marketing Cloud, and know how often it refreshes.
Know how data gets in: Batch ingestion, streaming, and reading data where it sits without copying it.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you bring customer data into Salesforce Data 360, model it, resolve it into one profile per person, then segment and activate it. Expect scenarios about matching records, mapping data and sending audiences to other systems.

keyConcepts.h2: Data Cloud Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: How Data 360 Works: Ingest, Model, Resolve, Segment, Activate
blocks.body: The whole product follows one path, and most exam questions sit somewhere on it. **Data streams** bring data in from a source such as Salesforce CRM, an S3 bucket, a website or a mobile app. The raw data lands in **data lake objects**. You then **map** those to **data model objects (DMOs)**, which are the shared shape Data 360 understands, for example Individual, Contact Point Email and Order. **Identity resolution** matches records that belong to the same person and builds a **unified profile**. **Segments** pick groups out of those profiles. **Activations** send a segment to a target system so it can be used in a campaign or a journey. If you can place a question on this path, the answer is usually easy to see.

blocks.heading: Identity Resolution: Match Rules and Reconciliation
blocks.body: Identity resolution runs in two steps. **Match rules** decide which records belong to the same person, for example an exact email match, a fuzzy name and address match, or a custom match on a loyalty ID. Several rules can run in order, and each one can catch records the previous one missed. **Reconciliation rules** then decide which value to keep when matched records disagree, for example 'most recently updated wins' or 'prefer the CRM source'. The result is one unified individual with links back to every source record. Watch for questions where a too-loose match rule merges two different people, which is the classic mistake.

blocks.heading: Segments and Activation
blocks.body: A **segment** is a group of unified profiles that match the filters you set, such as bought in the last 90 days and lives in Germany. Segments can use attributes from related objects and from calculated insights. They **refresh** on a schedule, so a segment is a living audience rather than a fixed list. An **activation** sends the segment to a target, such as Marketing Cloud, Advertising or an external system, and an **activation target** defines where it goes. You choose which attributes travel with it. Exam questions often turn on whether the data the marketer wants is actually available on the profile.

blocks.heading: Calculated Insights and Data Transforms
blocks.body: **Calculated insights** are metrics you define once and reuse, written in SQL, such as lifetime spend, average order value or days since last purchase. They can be used in segments, in activations and on the profile. **Data transforms** reshape data during or after ingestion, for example splitting a full name or converting currencies, so you do not have to fix the source system. Both matter on the exam because they are how you answer business questions that the raw data cannot answer on its own.

blocks.heading: Consent, Data Spaces and Governance
blocks.body: Customer data brings rules with it. Consent and privacy preferences are held against the individual, and activations should respect them. **Data spaces** keep data apart inside one Data 360 org, which is how you separate brands, regions or business units without buying another org. Permission sets control who can see and build what. Know which objects hold personal data, how deletion requests are handled, and why you would use a data space rather than filters to keep two brands separate.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Data Cloud Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Almost every question sits somewhere on the path from raw data to an activated audience. Work out which step the scenario is describing, then pick the tool that belongs to that step.

blocks.heading: Getting Data In
blocks.body: Batch ingestion for scheduled loads, streaming for events as they happen, and federated access when the data should stay in the source system.

blocks.heading: Identity Resolution
blocks.body: Match rules find the same person. Reconciliation rules choose which value wins. Loose match rules merge different people, which is the most common design error.

blocks.heading: Segmentation and Activation
blocks.body: Segments are living audiences that refresh on a schedule. Activations send them to a target with the attributes you choose.

blocks.heading: Calculated Insights
blocks.body: Use these for metrics like lifetime value or purchase frequency, then filter segments on them.

blocks.heading: Data Spaces and Permissions
blocks.body: Use data spaces to separate brands or regions. Use permission sets to control who can build segments and activations.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the primary purpose of Salesforce Data Cloud?
options: A CPQ pricing engine for enterprise contracts
Unifying customer data from multiple sources to create a real-time, actionable customer profile
A data warehouse for Salesforce backups only
An email marketing platform for batch campaign sends
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Cloud unifies data from multiple sources (Salesforce orgs, external systems, web, mobile) to create a single, actionable customer profile that drives segmentation, activation, and AI.
whyWrong: Data Cloud isn't a CPQ pricing engine, that's an entirely separate product category.
Data Cloud isn't a backup tool, it's built for real-time unified customer profiles, not just backup storage.
Data Cloud isn't an email marketing platform, that's Marketing Cloud's function.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Data Stream in Salesforce Data Cloud?
options: A connection that ingests data from a source system into Data Cloud, such as a Salesforce org, cloud storage, or external API
A real-time analytics dashboard that streams live sales data
A Marketing Cloud Journey that triggers based on Data Cloud segment membership
A scheduled Apex job that exports Data Cloud records to an external data warehouse
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Streams are the ingestion layer, each Data Stream connects to a data source and maps incoming data to Data Cloud Data Model Objects (DMOs).
whyWrong: A Data Stream doesn't itself provide analytics dashboards, that's a separate downstream capability, not the ingestion connection.
A Marketing Cloud Journey reacts to segments after they exist, it isn't the ingestion connection itself.
A scheduled Apex export job moves data out of Data Cloud, which is the opposite direction of what a Data Stream does (ingestion in).

sampleQuestions.question: What are Data Model Objects (DMOs) in Data Cloud?
options: Salesforce external objects that connect to a remote SOAP-based data source
Report types created for cross-object reporting in CRM Analytics
Custom fields on the Salesforce Lead object used to store data source metadata
Standardised tables in the Data Cloud data model that organise ingested data by category, such as Individual (person), Engagement, or other object types
sampleQuestions.explanation: DMOs are the structured tables in Data Cloud's canonical data model. Key DMOs include Individual (unified person record), Contact Point Email, Contact Point Phone, and various Engagement types.
whyWrong: External objects connect to remote systems via a different mechanism: DMOs are Data Cloud's own standardized data model tables.
CRM Analytics report types are a separate reporting concept, unrelated to Data Cloud's DMOs.
Custom Lead fields are a Salesforce Core concept, unrelated to Data Cloud's standardized DMO structure.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Identity Resolution do in Salesforce Data Cloud?
options: Validates that all incoming data complies with GDPR consent requirements before ingestion
Assigns unique Salesforce record IDs to Data Cloud profiles for CRM synchronisation
Links records from multiple data sources that belong to the same individual, creating a single unified profile by matching on email, phone, name, or custom rules
Authenticates external system API connections using OAuth 2.0 tokens
sampleQuestions.explanation: Identity Resolution applies matching and reconciliation rules to stitch together records from different sources into a single Unified Profile, resolving duplicate customer identities across channels.
whyWrong: GDPR consent validation is a separate compliance function, not what Identity Resolution itself does.
Assigning Salesforce record IDs is a CRM-specific concept, distinct from Data Cloud's cross-source identity matching.
OAuth 2.0 authentication is a separate technical mechanism, unrelated to matching person records across sources.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Unified Profile in Data Cloud?
options: A Salesforce Person Account record that merges duplicate contact records
A single, consolidated view of an individual that combines linked records from multiple sources after Identity Resolution has run
A custom report type that shows all interactions for a given Account
A Marketing Cloud subscriber profile enriched with Salesforce CRM data
sampleQuestions.explanation: After Identity Resolution links source records, a Unified Profile is created, providing a 360-degree view of the customer used for segmentation, activation, and AI grounding.
whyWrong: A Person Account is a specific Salesforce CRM record type, not the same as a Data Cloud Unified Profile concept.
A custom report type displays existing data, it doesn't itself create a consolidated unified view.
A Marketing Cloud subscriber profile is scoped to marketing data, not the full cross-source Unified Profile Data Cloud builds.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Segment in Data Cloud?
options: A Marketing Cloud List used to manage email subscription preferences
A dynamic audience of Unified Profiles that meet defined criteria, used for targeted activation across channels
A scheduled data export job that sends records to an external BI platform
A named permission set group that controls user access to Data Cloud features
sampleQuestions.explanation: Segments filter Unified Profiles by attribute criteria (e.g., purchase history, location, engagement) and are evaluated on a defined refresh schedule. Segments are the basis for activation.
whyWrong: A Marketing Cloud List manages subscription preferences, a Data Cloud Segment is a broader dynamic audience construct.
A scheduled export job moves data out, unrelated to defining a dynamic targeted audience.
A permission set group controls access, not audience targeting, that's a different concept from a Segment.

sampleQuestions.question: What is Activation in Salesforce Data Cloud?
options: Running Identity Resolution to create Unified Profiles from ingested data streams
Granting users permission to view and edit Data Cloud segments
Publishing segment membership to a destination system, such as Marketing Cloud, Advertising Studio, or a custom external platform, to drive campaigns and personalisation
Enabling Data Cloud in a Salesforce org for the first time through the Setup menu
sampleQuestions.explanation: Activation sends segment membership data and selected profile attributes to downstream systems so they can be used for campaigns, ad targeting, and personalisation.
whyWrong: Running Identity Resolution creates Unified Profiles, that's a separate step that happens before activation.
Granting segment view/edit permissions is an access-control concept, unrelated to publishing segments to destination systems.
Enabling Data Cloud is a one-time setup step, not the ongoing activation of segments to destinations.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Calculated Insight in Data Cloud?
options: A derived metric computed from Data Cloud data using SQL, such as total lifetime value, average order frequency, or days since last purchase, stored as an attribute on the Unified Profile
A Salesforce report metric automatically updated by a scheduled Apex job
An Einstein prediction score surfaced on a Salesforce record page via a formula field
A CRM Analytics widget that displays aggregated Data Cloud segment counts
sampleQuestions.explanation: Calculated Insights are SQL-based aggregations that enrich Unified Profiles with computed metrics, enabling segmentation and activation based on derived attributes like CLV or churn score.
whyWrong: A Salesforce report metric updated by Apex is a CRM Core concept, not the same as a Data Cloud SQL-derived attribute.
An Einstein prediction score surfaced via formula field is a different mechanism from a Calculated Insight computed within Data Cloud.
A CRM Analytics widget displays data, it doesn't itself compute the underlying derived metric.

sampleQuestions.question: Which consent mechanism does Data Cloud support for GDPR and CCPA compliance?
options: A Salesforce Shield encryption key that masks personal data for non-admin users
An Email Opt-Out field on the Marketing Cloud subscriber record that syncs to Data Cloud daily
Consent API and Individual's Privacy Attributes, allowing Data Cloud to respect opt-out and data deletion requests at the profile level across all ingested data
Manual record deletion performed by a Salesforce administrator on request
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Cloud honours consent through the Individual object's privacy attributes. Opt-outs and deletion requests propagate to prevent the use of suppressed profiles in segments and activations.
whyWrong: Shield encryption protects data at rest, it doesn't manage opt-out/deletion consent requests.
An Email Opt-Out field syncing daily is a narrower, marketing-specific mechanism, not the platform-wide consent API Data Cloud provides.
Manual deletion by an admin isn't a systematic, API-driven consent mechanism.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the role of a Data Cloud Consultant on an implementation project?
options: Designing the data ingestion architecture, configuring Identity Resolution, building segments, setting up activations, and advising customers on data governance strategy
Administering the Salesforce org's sharing model and permission sets for Data Cloud users
Writing Apex triggers to ingest data directly into Data Cloud from Salesforce Platform Events
Managing the Marketing Cloud account and creating email campaigns from Data Cloud segments
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Cloud Consultants lead the full data platform implementation, from source mapping and ingestion through to identity resolution, segmentation, activation, and governance advisory.
whyWrong: Administering sharing/permission sets is a general Salesforce admin task, not specific to Data Cloud consulting.
Writing Apex triggers for ingestion is a developer task, not the consultant's typical implementation-and-advisory role.
Managing Marketing Cloud campaigns is a narrower marketing execution task, not the broader Data Cloud consulting role described.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Data Action in Salesforce Data Cloud?
options: A custom validation rule that prevents incorrectly formatted records from being ingested
An automated Flow triggered when a new Data Stream ingestion job completes
A batch export job that sends Data Cloud records to an external data lake
A trigger that fires when a profile's segment membership changes, used to initiate downstream processes such as updating a Salesforce record or triggering a Marketing Cloud journey
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Actions respond to segment entry or exit events, enabling real-time orchestration, for example, creating a Salesforce Task when a customer enters a high-churn-risk segment.
whyWrong: A validation rule blocks bad data on entry, that's unrelated to triggering downstream processes on segment changes.
An ingestion-completion Flow trigger is a different event type from a segment-membership-change Data Action.
A batch export job moves data out on a schedule, it isn't the same as a real-time segment-membership-based trigger.

sampleQuestions.question: What distinguishes Salesforce Data Cloud from a traditional data warehouse?
options: Data Cloud is purpose-built for customer data unification, real-time segmentation, and AI grounding, with native Salesforce integration, Identity Resolution, and activation connectors that data warehouses do not provide out of the box
Data Cloud requires all data to be pre-processed in an ETL tool before ingestion, unlike data warehouses that accept raw data
Data Cloud stores data in relational tables exactly like a standard SQL database with no additional capabilities
Data Cloud cannot handle structured data; it is designed only for unstructured data such as call transcripts
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Cloud is a customer data platform (CDP), built for real-time profile unification, segmentation, and activation. Traditional data warehouses store and query data but lack native identity resolution, activation, and Salesforce CRM integration.
whyWrong: Data Cloud can ingest raw data directly, it doesn't require pre-processing through a separate ETL tool first.
Data Cloud has purpose-built capabilities well beyond a plain relational SQL database, this option denies its actual differentiators.
Data Cloud explicitly does handle structured data, this option incorrectly restricts it to unstructured data only.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Data Cloud object represents a unified person record across all sources?
options: Account
Segment
Contact Point Email only
Individual
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Individual DMO is the unified person record that Identity Resolution creates by stitching together data from multiple sources.
whyWrong: Account is a Salesforce CRM object, not the Data Cloud unified-person object.
Segment is a dynamic audience grouping, not the underlying unified person record itself.
Contact Point Email is one specific contact channel, not the full unified person record.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a Data Cloud Data Stream?
options: To create activation destinations
To run Calculated Insights
To connect a data source and map incoming records to DMOs for ingestion
To export segments
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Streams define the connection to a source (e.g., Salesforce, external API) and the mapping to Data Cloud objects.
whyWrong: Creating activation destinations is a separate configuration step from ingesting and mapping data via a Data Stream.
Running Calculated Insights happens after data is already ingested, it's not the Data Stream's function.
Exporting segments is a downstream activation step, not what a Data Stream does at ingestion.

sampleQuestions.question: How does Data Cloud support Einstein and Agentforce?
options: Only for Marketing Cloud
By providing unified profiles for grounding, enabling AI to access real customer data
Only for batch exports
It does not
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Cloud grounding lets Einstein and Agentforce access unified customer profiles for accurate, data-backed AI responses.
whyWrong: Grounding isn't Marketing-Cloud-only, it supports AI features across the Salesforce platform, including Agentforce.
Grounding isn't limited to batch exports, it's used for real-time AI context.
Data Cloud explicitly does support Einstein/Agentforce; 'it does not' denies a core integration point.
